links.outcome: AI fracture detection performance on difficult versus matched internal test sets
links.effect: Difficult set associated with 40% decreased odds of correct classification (OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.53-0.68) for EfficientNet and 80% decreased odds of detection (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.17-0.25) for YOLOv8.
links.quote: The difficult internal test set (392 patients, 786 radiographs) was associated with a 40% decrease in odds of a correct classification compared with the matched internal test set (526 patients, 786 radiographs) for EfficientNet variants (OR, 0.60 [95% CI: 0.53, 0.68]; P < .001).

screen.reason: Evaluates how test set composition and case-difficulty curation (a pre-deployment validation practice) impact observed AI performance in pediatric fracture detection.

primary.practice: stress testing on clinically difficult cases
